Gerald McBoing-Boing

UPA’s Oscar-winning short animated a Dr. Seuss story with flat, sparse drawings and limited movement, and set the look of mid-century “cartoon modern”.

Source
Wikipedia: Gerald McBoing-Boing
Creator
United Productions of America (UPA)
Made
1950 (released 4 November 1950)
Style
Mid-century modern (agent-proposed, not yet reviewed by a person)
Moods
Playful, sparse, modern
Evidence
Based on the Wikipedia article and its quotation from The New York Times. No frames of the film were inspected for this record.
Reviewed
28 September 2026
Rights
Link and metadata only. License: unverified. Rights policy

Context

Gerald McBoing-Boing is a 1950 animated short directed by Robert Cannon and produced by United Productions of America. Columbia Pictures released it on 4 November 1950. Phil Eastman and Bill Scott adapted a story by Dr. Seuss. Wikipedia.

It won the 1950 Academy Award for Best Animated Short. The Library of Congress selected it for the National Film Registry in 1995. Wikipedia.

Wikipedia quotes The New York Times: Cannon “was primarily responsible for the drawings, strongly reminiscent of a [Saul] Steinberg cartoon”, and Bill Hurtz and Herb Klynn did the design and the color. Wikipedia.

Why it belongs

UPA’s films moved studio animation away from rounded, fully animated characters toward flat, graphic drawing. That link between print illustration and motion is why the style record names limited animation as a trait.

Borrow

Animate by moving, cutting, and swapping flat shapes rather than by smooth tweening, as the style’s motion facet describes.

What to review next
